disposition_reason: Primary benchtop-XRF occurrence data for Pb, Cd, total As, total Hg and Al in 28 US small-beekeeper honeys from 15 states. Several printed values (Cd, Hg, Al means; Cd top values) contradict the paper's own figures and EWI column, and no LOD/CRM is reported, so only Pb and As figures are internally consistent.
disposition_locator: Methods 'Honey Samples' and Table 1 (pp. 1790-1791); Table 2 and Results (p. 1793); Figs 1-2 (p. 1792)

study.design: market survey (direct purchase from small-business beekeepers), multi-state
study.material_scope: Honey jars purchased from small-business beekeepers; Table 1 floral labels: Wildflower x19, Desert wildflower x1, Tupelo x2, and one each Turnip, Russian Olive, Sourwood, Star Thistle, Blueberry/Blackberry, Peach Flower (Methods: 'Twenty ... labeled as wildflower')
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Origin = state and zip code/locale on the beekeeper's label (15 states: AR 2, FL 2, IN 2, KY 4, ME 1, MD 1, MA 2, NM 4, NC 1, OK 1, OR 2, TN 3, TX 1, VT 1, WV 1). Purchased directly from those small-business beekeepers; retail channel/location of purchase not otherwise stated.
study.sampling_unit: honey samples (one per purchased honey); no replicates reported
study.method: Benchtop energy-dispersive XRF (Malvern Panalytical Epsilon 4, 50 kV, 300 uA, 7.5 min), undigested, unhomogenized honey in 30 mm cups under 4 um polypropylene film; calibration with doped phantoms and Compton-peak normalisation
study.basis: as-sold (fresh) honey, ug/g of material; no drying stated
study.qa: No CRM, recovery, or replicate data reported for honey; calibration validity cited to prior nail/bone/blood XRF work. Samples held in 1.5 mL plastic microcentrifuge tubes at room temperature in the dark until analysis.

controls.control: Apiary proximity to point sources (major highway)
controls.outcome: Authors suggest contamination may come from a single point source, e.g. the Boxboro, MA honey from within 5 km of Interstate-495; the high-metal Tennessee honey came from a very rural area with no major roadways or industry, so source unexplained. ArcGIS mapping found no distinct clustering of elevated toxic metals.

controls.control: EU limits used as benchmarks: Pb 0.10 mg/kg (Reg. (EU) 2023/915) and Hg 0.01 mg/kg (Reg. (EU) 2018/73, pesticide-residue MRL for mercury compounds); no US limits
controls.outcome: Paper states 'many'/'the vast majority' of honeys exceeded the EU Pb limit and many exceeded Hg; no counts printed. Fig 2 caption misstates the Pb line as 0.01 ug/g (text: 0.10). Visual reading of Fig 2a suggests roughly half of the 28 Pb points above 0.10; Fig 2c shows ~9 of 28 Hg points above zero.
controls.locator: Introduction p. 1790; Results p. 1793; Fig 2 caption p. 1792

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary says all four toxic metals and Al exceed JECFA PTWIs (e.g., Hg 501x). Recomputing the paper's stated formula (0.3 g honey/kg bw/day x conc x 7) gives values 1000x smaller than Table 2: e.g. Pb 0.178 mg/kg -> 0.00037 mg/kg bw/week (~1.5% of 0.025), As -> 0.00013 (vs 0.002), Hg (even at 3.71) -> 0.0078. The Table 2 EWIs are ug/kg bw/week mislabelled as mg; none exceed the PTWIs. The stored summary's claim that EWIs are 'internally consistent with the stated formula' is incorrect.

Stored summary treats Hg 3.710 and Al 64.36 as the means; the paper's own Fig 1 (Hg ~1.2, Al ~37 ug/g) and its EWI column (implying 1.19 and 36.8 ug/g) contradict both printed means. The summary flags only the Cd inconsistency.
Stored summary says 'the majority of samples exceeded EU MRLs for lead and mercury'. For Hg, Fig 2c shows ~19 of 28 honeys plotted at zero; the paper itself says only 'many' exceed the Hg limit.

Stored summary attributes '20 wildflower' to the Abstract and calls it a discrepancy; the 20 count is in Methods 'Honey Samples', and Table 1 lists 19 'Wildflower' plus 1 'Desert wildflower' (= 20), so it is consistent. The summary renders 'Desert wildflower' as 'desert flower'.
Stored summary places the '14 different states' wording in the Methods; it is in the Introduction (p. 1790).
Stored summary attributes Ti 0.056 ± 0.039 and V 0.021 ± 0.004 SEMs to the Results; those SEMs are from the Discussion (Results gives Ti ± 0.01, V ± 0.0). Non-scope elements; minor.
Stored summary's metals list omits Cr, which is measured and plotted in Fig 1a (mean ~0.11 ug/g visually; no number printed).
unresolved: True Cd, Hg and Al means are not printed consistently; figure- and EWI-implied values (~0.013, ~1.19, ~36.8 ug/g) are inferences, not printed results, so they are not recorded as findings.
Cd top-three values in text (TN 0.918, MA 0.820, VT 0.350 ug/g) are a copy error; real per-state Cd maxima are only readable from Fig 2b (~0.017 ug/g).
Per-state means (hash marks in Fig 2) and all other per-sample values exist only as plotted points; not digitised.
Cr (Fig 1a) has no printed numeric value.
No LOD/LOQ, CRM, recovery or replicate data; treatment of non-detects (plotted at 0) in the means is not stated.
Which of a state's samples produced each top value (zip code) is not identified.
XRF Hg values (up to 8.94 ug/g) are roughly 1000x typical honey literature levels and unverified by an independent method; treat with extreme caution.
Number of samples exceeding EU Pb/Hg limits is not printed.
